chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Umar ibn Aban al-Kalbi, from Abd al-Raheem al-Qasir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Every innovation is a straying, and every straying is in the Fire.'

key_terms.النَّارِ: al-nar — the Fire; the eschatological punishment assigned to those who deviate through innovation
key_terms.بِدْعَةٍ: bid'ah — any newly-introduced practice or belief with no basis in revelation or established prophetic sunnah
key_terms.ضَلَالَةٌ: dalalah — going astray, misguidance; deviation from the divinely-ordained straight path

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet Muhammad say about religious innovations (bid'ah) according to Imam al-Sadiq in al-Kafi?
ai.summary: This hadith, transmitted through Imam al-Sadiq (عليه السلام) and attributed to the Prophet (صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ), issues a sweeping condemnation of bid'ah — any addition to or alteration of revealed religion. The two-part prophetic declaration first equates innovation with misguidance, then anchors that misguidance to eschatological punishment in the Fire, making the warning absolute and unconditional. Preserved in al-Kulayni's chapter on bid'ah, ra'y, and analogies, this hadith serves as one of the foremost textual authorities in Shia jurisprudence against unwarranted religious novelty.
